topic_tag: fate of a dissolved guild's hall
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.

worlds.passage: A weavers' guild built a stone hall beside the market square of a river town in 1580, and the guild was dissolved in 1760. The hall stood on the only ground in the town above the river's high-water mark. Parish records show the lower streets under water in the springs of 1784, 1802 and 1830, and for several weeks in each of those years the council's accounts list bread, straw and lamp oil delivered to the hall. In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.
worlds.explanation: Standing above the high-water mark, the hall received bread, straw and lamp oil for weeks whenever the lower streets flooded, which means it housed the flooded families, so it served as the town's "refuge." "Platform" fails because the supplies point to people staying in the hall, not speaking from it. "Ornament" fails because its value lay in its high ground, not its appearance. "Quarry" fails because the building stayed whole and in use.

platform.quote: bread, straw and lamp oil delivered to the hall
platform.why: the supplies are for people staying in the hall, not for anyone addressing the public from it

ornament.why: the hall mattered for where it stood when the town flooded, not for its looks

quarry.quote: for several weeks in each of those years
quarry.why: the hall was in use as a building through 1830, so it was not being broken up for stone

worlds.passage: A weavers' guild built a stone hall beside the market square of a river town in 1580, and the guild was dissolved in 1760. Its long balcony looked down on the square, which farmers from every village in the district crowded into on market days. In the weeks before each council election, the weekly paper's accounts of what the candidates had promised were written by reporters standing in the square below it. In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.
worlds.explanation: The balcony overlooked the crowded square, and before each election reporters stood beneath it to take down the candidates' promises, so the candidates spoke from it and the hall served as the town's "platform." "Refuge" fails because no one sheltered in the hall. "Ornament" fails because the hall mattered for what was said from it, not its looks. "Quarry" fails because the balcony stayed in use election after election.

refuge.why: the hall's role concerns the crowd gathered in front of it, not anyone sheltering inside

ornament.why: what mattered about the hall was what was heard from its balcony, not its appearance

quarry.quote: In the weeks before each council election
quarry.why: the balcony was in use at every election, so the building stood intact rather than being stripped for stone

worlds.passage: A weavers' guild built a stone hall beside the market square of a river town in 1580, and the guild was dissolved in 1760. The council repainted its carved front after every hard winter and hung it with lamps on feast days. Its accounts for those hundred years record the cost of the paint, the lamps and the roof and nothing else, and an inventory of 1850 found the building's keys rusted to their hook in the clerk's office. In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.
worlds.explanation: The council paid to keep the hall's front painted and lit while its keys sat unused for years, so it served the town chiefly as an "ornament," kept up only to be looked at. "Refuge" fails because the building was never opened. "Platform" fails because the council's spending covered only upkeep and display, with no gatherings. "Quarry" fails because the hall was carefully maintained, not broken up.

refuge.why: a building whose keys had not been used in years sheltered no one

platform.quote: the paint, the lamps and the roof and nothing else
platform.why: the council spent on the building's appearance and upkeep only; nothing suggests it was used for addressing anyone

quarry.quote: repainted its carved front after every hard winter
quarry.why: the building was being preserved, not stripped for its stone

worlds.passage: A weavers' guild built a stone hall beside the market square of a river town in 1580, and the guild was dissolved in 1760. No buyer could be found for the building, and within forty years it had lost its roof and most of its upper walls. A survey of the town in 1860 found carved blocks bearing a weaver's shuttle in the foundations of more than sixty houses and in the bridge over the millrace. In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.
worlds.explanation: The weavers' hall lost its walls while blocks carved with a weaver's shuttle turned up in houses and a bridge across town, so it served as the town's "quarry," a source of building stone. "Refuge" fails because a roofless ruin sheltered no one. "Platform" fails because no one spoke from the hall. "Ornament" fails because the hall was left to fall apart, and its carving survived only in foundations.

refuge.quote: lost its roof and most of its upper walls
refuge.why: a building without a roof or walls could shelter no one

platform.why: the building stood unused and decaying; nothing suggests anyone addressed the public from it

ornament.quote: in the foundations of more than sixty houses
ornament.why: the carved stones ended up buried in foundations, used as material, not displayed
